subject: Re: Annual commit tiers — alternative slab + blended credits proposal
body:
From: Elena Torres <elena@brightscale.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightscale.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual commit tiers question and proposed blended credits

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency figures and caching behavior look promising for our pipeline. We're starting to model a committed plan for next year and have a few packaging/questions before we put together the internal business case. Quick context:
- Current expected usage: ~18M tokens/month for Q1 2027, with a projected ramp to ~60M tokens/month by Q4 2027 (inference heavy).
- Primary goal: predictable unit cost while keeping the option to scale quickly for spikes.

Specific asks:
1) Can you share a concise overview of how Redwood defines the Starter / Growth / Enterprise commit tiers (token bands and typical per-token discounts)?
2) Do you offer a blended-credits approach (mix of committed discounted tokens + on-demand at a higher rate) and how is overage billed?
3) Any flexibility for a staged ramp (e.g., firm commit at lower tier for months 1–3 with automatic re-eval at quarter boundaries)?
4) What are typical contract lengths you’ve seen (12 vs 24) and how you handle early termination credits?

We have attached a draft SOW for scope so you can map pricing to the integrations. Appreciate something concise — we need internal procurement language for our finance review.

Attachment: BrightScale_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Thanks,
Elena
--
Elena Torres
Head of Platform
BrightScale Analytics
elena@brightscale.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightscale.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers question and proposed blended credits

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear context and the SOW. Looping in Priyom (account lead) and Vivek (pricing) to propose a concise option set. High-level answers now, detailed numbers to follow in a short spreadsheet: 

- Tier definitions (short):
  * Starter: up to 10M tokens/mo committed — suitable for proof-of-concepts and small pilots.
  * Growth: 10M–40M tokens/mo committed — typical for growing product teams.
  * Enterprise: 40M+ tokens/mo committed — for high-volume production workloads with SLA add-ons.

- Blended credits: yes — we commonly structure a committed discounted tranche + an on-demand pool billed at standard hosted rate. We can create a blended effective $/token example tied to your expected ramp. Overage billing is monthly; overages above committed tokens are billed at the on-demand rate unless you opt into a grace buffer or pre-purchased burst credits.

- Staged ramp: we offer staged ramp clauses (quarterly re-eval and automatic tier bump if usage consistently exceeds threshold) and fallback credits for burst months.

- Term length: most customers pick 12 or 24 months. 12-month is standard for early-stage deals; 24-months gets modest additional discounts and more flexible billing cadence. Early termination typically involves a remaining-commit true-up or a short credit schedule — we can propose language.

Priyom / Vivek — can you prepare a 2-tab spreadsheet (1: tier prices + blended examples keyed to Elena's ramp, 2: SOW redline highlights) and a short note on quantization/embedding pricing differences? Elena — any preference on term (12 vs 24) and billing cadence (monthly/quarterly)?

— Priya
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@brightscale.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers question and proposed blended credits

Adding quick thoughts from the AM side — putting myself in BrightScale's shoes given the ramp: 
1) Recommend a Growth-tier anchor for Q1 (commit 12–15M tokens/mo) with an automated review at the end of Q2 to re-base to Enterprise if utilization >45M consistently.
2) Suggest a blended credits structure: commit 60% of expected tokens at a discounted slab and leave 40% as on-demand/burst. That gives BrightScale predictability but preserves headroom.
3) For procurement: offer Net 30 invoicing with quarterly checks. If finance insists on annual prepayment we can show an extra 6–8% discount.

If pricing agrees, I can drive a short SOW redline and set up a customer call.

— Priyom
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@brightscale.ai>, procurement@brightscale.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing matrix + blended example (BrightScale model)

Elena / team — attached is a compact pricing-model-alt.xlsx with:
- Tab A: Commit slab prices ($/1k tokens) for Starter/Growth/Enterprise with suggested discounts vs on-demand.
- Tab B: Blended example using BrightScale's ramp (18M -> 60M) showing effective $/token and monthly invoice scenarios.
- Tab C: Overage rules, fallback credits, and quantization uplift assumptions.

Highlights (summary):
- Suggested committed nominal rates (per 1k tokens):
  * Starter (<=10M/mo): $0.90 per 1k tokens
  * Growth (10–40M/mo): $0.58 per 1k tokens
  * Enterprise (40M+): $0.35 per 1k tokens (SLA + support add-on)
- Blended example (Q1 ramp to 18M): if BrightScale commits 12M and leaves 6M as on-demand, blended effective = ~$0.72/1k tokens for month 1.
- For months with spikes we propose a 10% burst credit buffer for first 3 months to smooth onboarding spikes.
- Term incentive: move to a 24-month contract to receive an additional ~6% off committed rates and priority capacity during peak maintenance windows.

Open items for procurement: whether they want annual prepay vs monthly invoice, and whether they want the SOW to include a minimum performance SLA clause.

Attachment: pricing-model-alt.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

Let me know if you want a third column showing quantized int8/4 runs and the associated uplift (typical 12–20% token efficiency, lower $/token).

— Vivek
Pricing & Packaging
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Elena — attaching the short spreadsheet Vivek prepared and a one-paragraph summary for your procurement team (below). Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call early next week to walk the numbers and SOW redlines.

Summary we propose for BrightScale:
- Initial anchor: Growth commit of 12M tokens/month for first quarter (12-month term, Net 30 billing).
- Blended approach: 60% committed at Growth slab rate, 40% on-demand. Effective blended $/1k tokens ~ $0.72 in Q1 given your ramp.
- Spike protection: 10% buffer credits for first 90 days; monthly overages bill at on-demand after buffer.
- Operational items: quarterly usage review with automatic tier bump when 45M+ sustained for 2 months; optional 24-month prepay for an additional 6% concession.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred term (12 vs 24) and billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
2) If approved, I’ll circulate a redlined SOW (one page) and a short signature-ready amendment covering commit bands and overage rules.
3) We can schedule a 30-min call — suggest Tue 11/2 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 11/3 9:00–9:30 PT.

Attachment: pricing-model-alt.xlsx

Thanks,
